official.description: ACIAR's Pacific postgraduate scholarships are offered in the Pacific, to Pacific Islanders, enabling scholars to research agricultural problems within the context where the solutions need to work; the PASS Program aims to strengthen the Pacific agricultural innovation system through the strengths of Pacific universities and their regional partners.
official.english_requirement: The medium of instruction at FNU is the English language; HDR students must be sufficiently fluent and provide evidence from undergraduate or other English qualifications confirming English language competency. No test score is published.

applicant_utility.summary: PASS funds Pacific Island nationals to undertake agriculture, forestry and related research degrees at Fiji National University without leaving the region, pairing each scholar with an ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor so the research plugs into a live ACIAR project. The package is concrete: full tuition, a FJD 21,450 yearly living allowance (FJD 32,472 if accompanied), one-off book and establishment allowances, medical insurance, and a research grant of up to FJD 17,500 for Masters or FJD 40,000 for PhD. The application is more than a form: you must settle a research topic with both FNU and ACIAR supervisors and submit before 5pm FJT on 21 October 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Pacific Island nationals aged 35 or under (45 for PhD) with a relevant bachelor's or postgraduate degree who want a research degree in agriculture or forestry at home in the region.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the ACIAR Graduate Officer (aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj) to check eligibility before doing any paperwork
Choose a research direction and identify the matching FNU supervisor and ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor early
Draft the research intent with both supervisors and obtain their signatures
Assemble transcripts, certificates and citizenship evidence into one complete package before deadline day
common_rejection_risks: Applying without first checking eligibility with the ACIAR Graduate Officer
A research topic not agreed with both the FNU supervisor and the ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor
GPA shortfalls against the stated thresholds (3.0 for MSc Agriculture/Forestry; 3.5 for a coursework bachelor's; 4.0 for coursework master's or Honours routes)
Age over the 35/45 limit without an exceptional-case argument
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living allowance rates are fixed (FJD 21,450 p.a. unaccompanied; FJD 32,472 p.a. accompanied), so family costs beyond the accompanied rate, relocation beyond the establishment allowance and personal expenses are self-funded; the establishment allowance applies only 'if applicable'.
document_audit: The research intent must be signed by the FNU supervisor and the relevant co-supervisor - unsigned forms stall
Academic transcripts, certificates and evidence of citizenship must be complete and legible
Use the current 2027 application form and Research Intent Form downloaded from the FNU page
English competency is evidenced through undergraduate or other English qualifications, not an external test - keep those transcripts handy
alerts: Applications opened 20 August 2026 and close at 5pm FJT on Wednesday 21 October 2026 for Graduate Term 1 2027
Accompanied applicants are paid a different living allowance - declare status correctly at application
The award is tied to specific FNU programmes: MSc Agriculture (thesis), MSc Forestry (thesis), Masters by Research or PhD
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Check eligibility with the ACIAR Graduate Officer, agree the topic with FNU and ACIAR supervisors, then email the completed application form, signed research intent and supporting documents to aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj before the 5pm FJT close.
